questions.prompt: In the Roofline paper, operational intensity divides operations by what?
options: Loads and stores in the source code
Bytes of DRAM traffic, after the caches
questions.explanation: DRAM traffic, so the same algorithm can have different intensity depending on cache behaviour.

questions.prompt: What does a compute ceiling below the roof represent?
options: The performance limit if a specific optimisation (e.g. SIMD or ILP) is missing
questions.explanation: Ceilings tell you which optimisation would lift a kernel stuck beneath them.

questions.prompt: A kernel does 3 × 10⁹ FLOPs and moves 1.5 × 10⁹ bytes of DRAM traffic on the GW-1 (1,536 GFLOP/s, 512 GB/s). What's its attainable GFLOP/s?
Why might a machine with a ridge point far to the right be 'hard to use'?
options: Only kernels with very high intensity can reach its peak compute
questions.explanation: Most kernels sit left of a far-right ridge and can only use a fraction of peak compute.

questions.prompt: Where is the roofline used today?
options: Deciding whether ML layers are compute- or memory-bound
Choosing a GPU's clock frequency at run time
questions.explanation: It's a design and analysis model; it doesn't control clocks.
